cases.reason: The setup isolates a legend, kin or gift and invokes the explicit transition: waves do not wake legends, kin restore sleep, only a placed sigil completes a quest at any age, no buff is awarded, and the 100-letter Easter egg has its own tether/release rules. Fixed steps here check the declared state/timer/boundary, not an uncontrolled win rate. The staggered five-second kin check is a per-frame work bound. Early-quest wording still says baby, but its assertion explicitly says any age; it does not enforce the retired age requirement. Known-quest and offering policies receive fabricated observations/stack acknowledgements and explicit deadlines; they cannot invent unseen cues. Ending cases advance only the wave/ending clock and force neutralization, checking automatic ending and observed/drawn-pointer agreement, not whether a bot wins a natural night. Dream helpers directly check nearest-kind/compass results and quest-open flags. Slow-time tests force ring entry/exit, held headings and a boundary-crossing letter: clock-rate scaling and exclusion remain direct rules, despite numeric movement checks, rather than sampled battle outcomes.

supersessionCandidates.quote: Journal backpressure (#1559, 2026-11-01): flush requests share one active drain and one current pending set. A blocked storage write no longer captures a new batch for each request. Deletions are reconciled against committed row IDs, so never-committed debug evictions do not accumulate deletion IDs. The blocked-store regression reduced 101 writes to two while retaining the error and latest debug row; this is a storage-stub result, not browser latency or a renderer-crash explanation. Warning/error retention remains exempt from the low-priority cap.

cases.name: runs at its tempo, and turns beats back into times
cases.fullName: beat clock > runs at its tempo, and turns beats back into times
cases.reason: The planner receives synthetic wave clocks; the score receives explicit seeds and styles. Assertions directly implement the 9 Oct ABAC structure, 11 Oct nightly set and 14 Oct alto/stepwise redesign. A 30-minute planner loop is not a played night. The 120 BPM test supplies its own style-based beat tuning; it does not prohibit choosing a different record. Wide instrument phrases, retained soprano fallback and alternate lab arpeggios are explicit comparison modes, not stale default singer claims. Additional beat/DJ/knockdown tests use specified clocks and tuning, including explicit bpmStep1/cap5 comparison parameters. Their real wave integration checks the derived tempo/countdown ratio, not an emergent win target. Beat inverse/continuity and DJ stroke order remain direct contracts. Two monolithic music tests explicitly set position/time/speaker damage and call musicMix; they do not simulate sampled sound success.

Those are direct contracts even when numeric or stepped.

supersessionCandidates.quote: - **The creature-state model** (issue #87, Ed 2026-10-05, via the coordinator): the witch does no damage; she only invites. Wild becomes happy by inviting (it defends its own area, never enraged); leashing a happy one is a second step, and only leashed ones grow (on berries). cases.reason: Most inputs are fabricated rows/configs. Screen tests validate frozen experiment controls and gate text, not whether a bot wins. Toy ask/tell scores protect resumability. Tiny real expert-contract cases assert provenance, replay equality and honest unsupported results. The inventory classifier tests pass strings like advance(world); they never advance a world.
